title: 1 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 2.

questions.question: What did David charge Solomon to be as he approached the end of his life?
options: Be strong and show thyself a man
Be wise and humble
Be rich and powerful
Be a priest and prophet
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and show thyself a man
questions.explanation: David charged Solomon saying, 'be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man' as stated in 1 Kings 2:2.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 2, what is the reason Solomon should keep the charge of the LORD?
options: So that he may prosper in all that he doeth
So that he may become king
So that he will be wealthy
So that he will have many children
questions.correctAnswer: So that he may prosper in all that he doeth
questions.explanation: David told Solomon to keep the charge of the LORD 'that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself,' according to 1 Kings 2:3.

questions.question: What did David say would happen if his children walked before God in truth with all their heart and soul?
options: There shall not fail a man on the throne of Israel
They would be rich and famous
They would defeat all enemies
They would never face hardship
questions.correctAnswer: There shall not fail a man on the throne of Israel
questions.explanation: David said if his children walked before God in truth, 'there shall not fail thee a man on the throne of Israel,' as in 1 Kings 2:4.

questions.question: Who did David remind Solomon had killed two captains of the hosts of Israel, Abner and Amasa?
options: Joab the son of Zeruiah
Adonijah the son of Haggith
Abiathar the priest
Shimei the son of Gera
questions.correctAnswer: Joab the son of Zeruiah
questions.explanation: David reminded Solomon about Joab killing Abner and Amasa in 1 Kings 2:5.

questions.question: What instruction did David give Solomon regarding Joab's fate?
options: Let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace
Spare him and show mercy
Make him your chief captain
Send him to exile
questions.correctAnswer: Let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace
questions.explanation: David instructed Solomon to not let Joab's hoar head go down to the grave in peace, as in 1 Kings 2:6.

questions.question: Who did David tell Solomon to show kindness to because they had helped him when he fled Absalom?
options: The sons of Barzillai the Gileadite
Joab the son of Zeruiah
Adonijah the son of Haggith
Shimei the son of Gera
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of Barzillai the Gileadite
questions.explanation: David told Solomon to show kindness unto the sons of Barzillai because they came to him when he fled from Absalom, as stated in 1 Kings 2:7.

questions.question: What oath did David swear to Shimei when he came down to meet him at Jordan?
options: I will not put thee to death with the sword
I will make thee my advisor
I will banish thee from Jerusalem
I will give thee riches and land
questions.correctAnswer: I will not put thee to death with the sword
questions.explanation: David swore to Shimei by the LORD that he would not put him to death with the sword, according to 1 Kings 2:8.

questions.question: True or False: David told Solomon to hold Shimei guiltless and let him live in peace.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: David told Solomon to not hold Shimei guiltless but to bring his hoar head down to the grave with blood, as in 1 Kings 2:9.

questions.question: How many years did David reign in Jerusalem according to 1 Kings 2?
options: Thirty and three years
Seven years
Forty years
Twenty years
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty and three years
questions.explanation: David reigned thirty and three years in Jerusalem, as stated in 1 Kings 2:11.

questions.question: Who came to Bathsheba asking if he came peaceably?
options: Adonijah the son of Haggith
Joab the son of Zeruiah
Shimei the son of Gera
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
questions.correctAnswer: Adonijah the son of Haggith
questions.explanation: Adonijah came to Bathsheba and she asked if he came peaceably, as in 1 Kings 2:13.

questions.question: What did Adonijah request from Bathsheba to ask Solomon for?
options: To give him Abishag the Shunammite to wife
To make him king
To pardon Joab
To exile Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: To give him Abishag the Shunammite to wife
questions.explanation: Adonijah asked Bathsheba to request Solomon to give him Abishag the Shunammite to wife, as stated in 1 Kings 2:17.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon agreed immediately to give Abishag the Shunammite to Adonijah as a wife.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Solomon questioned why Adonijah asked for Abishag and implied it was a dangerous request, as in 1 Kings 2:22.

questions.question: What did Solomon swear concerning Adonijah after hearing his request?
options: Adonijah shall be put to death this day
Adonijah shall be made a prince
Adonijah shall be pardoned
Adonijah shall be sent into exile
questions.correctAnswer: Adonijah shall be put to death this day
questions.explanation: Solomon swore that Adonijah would be put to death that day, according to 1 Kings 2:24.

questions.question: True or False: David was buried in the city of David after he died.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David as stated in 1 Kings 2:10.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 2, which instruction comes first?
options: Be strong and show thyself a man
Show kindness to the sons of Barzillai
Bring Joab's hoar head down to the grave
Deal with Shimei according to wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Be strong and show thyself a man
questions.explanation: David's first instruction to Solomon was to be strong and show himself a man in 1 Kings 2:2 before giving other commands.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What was Adonijah's request to Bathsheba for Solomon to consider?
options: That he be made king instead of Solomon
That Abishag the Shunammite be given to him as a wife
That Joab be spared
That Abiathar be restored as priest
questions.correctAnswer: That Abishag the Shunammite be given to him as a wife
questions.explanation: Adonijah asked Bathsheba to speak to King Solomon to give him Abishag the Shunammite as a wife (1 Kings 2:17, 1 Kings 2:21). This was his one petition after recognizing Solomon's kingship.

questions.question: How did Solomon respond to Bathsheba's request for Adonijah to have Abishag the Shunammite?
options: He granted the request without hesitation
He questioned why she asked for Abishag and reminded her of Adonijah's claim to the kingdom
He ignored the request and changed the subject
He gave Abishag to another man
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned why she asked for Abishag and reminded her of Adonijah's claim to the kingdom
questions.explanation: Solomon responded by asking why she would request Abishag for Adonijah and told her to ask also for the kingdom, reminding her that Adonijah was his elder brother (1 Kings 2:22).

questions.question: What was the consequence Solomon declared for Adonijah after hearing his request?
options: Adonijah would be made co-regent with Solomon
Adonijah would be exiled to another kingdom
Adonijah would be put to death that day
Adonijah would become priest
questions.correctAnswer: Adonijah would be put to death that day
questions.explanation: Solomon swore by the LORD and declared that Adonijah would be put to death the same day for speaking against his own life (1 Kings 2:23, 1 Kings 2:24).

questions.question: Why did Solomon spare Abiathar the priest from death at that time?
options: Because Abiathar was Joab's relative
Because Abiathar had been faithful to him
Because Abiathar had carried the ark before David and shared in his afflictions
Because Abiathar was old and weak
questions.correctAnswer: Because Abiathar had carried the ark before David and shared in his afflictions
questions.explanation: Solomon spared Abiathar because he had borne the ark of the Lord before David and had been afflicted in all that David was afflicted (1 Kings 2:26).

questions.question: What did Solomon do to fulfill the word of the LORD concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh?
options: He made Abiathar high priest
He cast Abiathar out from being priest unto the LORD
He built a temple for Abiathar
He sent Abiathar to lead Israel's army
questions.correctAnswer: He cast Abiathar out from being priest unto the LORD
questions.explanation: Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest to fulfill the LORD's word concerning the house of Eli (1 Kings 2:27).

questions.question: What action did Joab take when he heard of Solomon's intentions against him?
options: He fled to Egypt
He hid in the wilderness
He fled to the tabernacle of the LORD and caught hold of the horns of the altar
He surrendered to Solomon
questions.correctAnswer: He fled to the tabernacle of the LORD and caught hold of the horns of the altar
questions.explanation: Joab fled to the tabernacle of the LORD and caught hold of the horns of the altar seeking refuge (1 Kings 2:28).

questions.question: How did King Solomon instruct Benaiah regarding Joab's refuge at the altar?
options: To let Joab live because he was seeking sanctuary
To bring Joab before the king for trial
To fall upon Joab and kill him, then bury him
To exile Joab to another land
questions.correctAnswer: To fall upon Joab and kill him, then bury him
questions.explanation: Solomon ordered Benaiah to kill Joab at the altar and bury him, to remove innocent blood from the king and his house (1 Kings 2:29, 1 Kings 2:31).

questions.question: Why did Solomon say that the blood of Abner and Amasa would return upon Joab's head?
options: Because Joab was innocent of their deaths
Because Joab killed them without David's knowledge though they were more righteous
Because Joab was their ally
Because Joab was appointed by them
questions.correctAnswer: Because Joab killed them without David's knowledge though they were more righteous
questions.explanation: Solomon declared that Joab would bear the guilt because he slew Abner and Amasa, who were more righteous and better than he, and David did not know about it (1 Kings 2:32).

questions.question: What position did Solomon give to Benaiah after Joab was slain?
options: High priest
Captain over the host
Advisor to the king
Governor of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Captain over the host
questions.explanation: After Joab's death, Solomon appointed Benaiah as captain over the host, replacing Joab (1 Kings 2:35).

questions.question: What instructions did Solomon give to Shimei regarding his residence?
options: To leave Jerusalem immediately
To build a house in Jerusalem and not leave it
To go into exile in Gath
To serve in the army
questions.correctAnswer: To build a house in Jerusalem and not leave it
questions.explanation: Solomon commanded Shimei to build a house in Jerusalem, dwell there, and not go out anywhere else under penalty of death (1 Kings 2:36, 1 Kings 2:37).

questions.question: What was the result when Shimei's servants fled to Gath and he went to retrieve them?
options: He was praised by Solomon for loyalty
He was killed by the king's men
Solomon confronted Shimei for breaking his oath
He was made a general
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon confronted Shimei for breaking his oath
questions.explanation: When Shimei left Jerusalem to retrieve his servants, Solomon called him and questioned why he broke his oath, warning him of the consequences (1 Kings 2:41-2:44).

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 2:24 promise will happen if Solomon remains faithful to the LORD as David did?
options: Adonijah will be king
The house of David will be established forever
Abiathar will be priest again
The kingdom will be divided
questions.correctAnswer: The house of David will be established forever
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:24 asserts that Solomon's reign, established by the LORD as with David, will fulfill the promise of an enduring house if faithfulness is maintained (connected also with 1 Kings 2:4 about the throne not failing).

questions.question: How does Solomon’s handling of Adonijah’s request demonstrate the biblical virtue of justice?
options: By granting all requests regardless of consequences
By ignoring requests from family members
By upholding the rightful kingship and punishing rebellion
By showing favoritism to Adonijah
questions.correctAnswer: By upholding the rightful kingship and punishing rebellion
questions.explanation: Solomon acted justly by affirming the LORD's appointment of his kingship and ordering the death of Adonijah, who had rebelled, showing justice in leadership (1 Kings 2:22-2:25).

questions.question: True or False: Solomon showed kindness to the sons of Barzillai as David had instructed.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David instructed Solomon to show kindness to the sons of Barzillai for their loyalty, and Solomon honored this charge (1 Kings 2:7).

questions.question: True or False: Solomon spared Joab’s life because he was loyal to David.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Solomon ordered Joab's death because Joab had killed two men more righteous than himself, despite his loyalty to David; thus, he was not spared (1 Kings 2:31-2:34).

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 2.

questions.question: What consequence did Solomon assign to Joab for the blood he shed against two more righteous men, according to 1 Kings 2?
options: Joab would be forgiven because David did not know
Joab’s blood and that of his descendants would return upon them forever
Joab would be banished from Israel
Joab would be made captain of the host
questions.correctAnswer: Joab’s blood and that of his descendants would return upon them forever
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:33 states that the blood of Joab and his seed shall return upon their own heads forever because he slew two men more righteous than himself.

questions.question: Who killed Joab as commanded by King Solomon?
options: Abiathar
Zadok
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
Adonijah
questions.correctAnswer: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:34 records that Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went and fell upon Joab and slew him as commanded by Solomon.

questions.question: What position did Solomon give to Benaiah after Joab’s death?
options: High Priest
Captain over the host
Chief counselor
Governor of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Captain over the host
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 2:35, Solomon appointed Benaiah the son of Jehoiada in Joab’s room over the host.

questions.question: What was Solomon’s command to Shimei regarding where he should live?
options: Build a house in Jerusalem and not go out anywhere else
Live in the wilderness without a house
Go to Gath and serve King Achish
Return to his ancestral fields in Anathoth
questions.correctAnswer: Build a house in Jerusalem and not go out anywhere else
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:36 records that Solomon told Shimei to build a house in Jerusalem and dwell there, not going elsewhere.

questions.question: What warning did Solomon give Shimei about leaving Jerusalem and crossing the brook Kidron?
options: He would be crowned king
He would surely die and his blood would be on his own head
He would find favor in the eyes of Solomon
He would be sent into exile
questions.correctAnswer: He would surely die and his blood would be on his own head
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:37 states that if Shimei goes out and crosses the brook Kidron, he will surely die and his blood will be upon his own head.

questions.question: True or False: Shimei obeyed Solomon’s command by staying in Jerusalem many days without leaving.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:38 states that Shimei said the saying was good and dwelt in Jerusalem many days as commanded.

questions.question: What caused Shimei to leave Jerusalem despite the king's warning?
options: He wanted to reclaim his kingdom
Two of his servants ran away to Gath
He was summoned by King Achish
He sought to join Adonijah's rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: Two of his servants ran away to Gath
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:39-40 describe that two servants of Shimei fled to Gath, prompting Shimei to go and bring them back.

questions.question: How did Solomon respond when he learned Shimei had left Jerusalem and returned?
options: He praised Shimei for his loyalty
He ignored it
He summoned Shimei and questioned him about breaking his oath
He rewarded Shimei with more land
questions.correctAnswer: He summoned Shimei and questioned him about breaking his oath
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:41-43 recount Solomon calling for Shimei, reminding him of his oath and asking why he did not keep it.

questions.question: What did Solomon say would happen to Shimei because of his past wickedness against David?
options: He would be made priest
The LORD would return his wickedness upon his own head
He would be forgiven and restored
He would be made captain of the host
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD would return his wickedness upon his own head
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 2:44, Solomon declares that the LORD shall return Shimei’s wickedness upon his own head due to his actions against David.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon’s throne and house would be established before the LORD forever as a result of his actions against his enemies.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:45 confirms that Solomon will be blessed and the throne of David established before the LORD forever.

questions.question: Who executed Shimei after Solomon’s command?
options: Zadok the priest
Abiathar
Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
Adonijah
questions.correctAnswer: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:46 states that Benaiah went out and fell upon Shimei, killing him as Solomon commanded.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of divine justice and retribution as seen in Solomon's judgment against Joab and Shimei?
options: Psalm 7
Proverbs 3
Genesis 12
Exodus 20
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 7
questions.explanation: Psalm 7 contains pleas for the LORD to bring justice upon the wicked, paralleling Solomon’s actions to uphold divine justice (1 Kings 2:33-46).

questions.question: The removal of Abiathar from the priesthood in 1 Kings 2:27 fulfills a prophecy concerning which priestly family?
options: The family of Levi
The house of Eli
The descendants of Aaron
The sons of Zadok
questions.correctAnswer: The house of Eli
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 2:27 states Solomon thrust out Abiathar to fulfill the word of the LORD concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh, as prophesied in 1 Samuel 2:27-36.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word meaning 'old man' or 'hoar head' is significant in the context of Solomon's orders against Joab and Shimei?
options: Zaken
Tzaddik
Rashah
Chesed
questions.correctAnswer: Zaken
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'zaken' (זקן) means 'old man' or 'hoar head' and is used in 1 Kings 2:6 and 2:9 regarding Joab’s punishment.

questions.question: What literary device does the narrative of Shimei’s oath and eventual punishment best exemplify in 1 Kings 2?
options: Chiasmus
Foreshadowing
Inclusio
Parallelism
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The story of Shimei is framed by his oath to remain in Jerusalem (2:38) and his breaking of that oath leading to death (2:46), creating an inclusio that brackets his narrative.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What primary command did David give Solomon concerning his conduct before God to ensure prosperity?
options: To walk in the ways of the LORD and keep His commandments
To build a temple for the LORD
To conquer all surrounding nations
To appoint priests and judges immediately
questions.correctAnswer: To walk in the ways of the LORD and keep His commandments
questions.explanation: David charged Solomon to keep the charge of the LORD by walking in His ways, keeping His statutes, commandments, judgments, and testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that he may prosper wherever he goes (1 Kings 2:3).

questions.question: According to David's charge to Solomon, what condition ensures that no man will fail on the throne of Israel?
options: If Solomon builds a strong army
If Solomon's children walk before God in truth with all their heart and soul
If Solomon collects tribute from all nations
If Solomon marries a foreign princess
questions.correctAnswer: If Solomon's children walk before God in truth with all their heart and soul
questions.explanation: David reminds Solomon that the LORD's word promised that if his children take heed to their way and walk before God in truth with all their heart and soul, no man shall fail on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 2:4).

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by Solomon's execution of Adonijah and removal of Abiathar, as commanded by David and carried out by Solomon?
options: Divine judgment and the enforcement of covenant faithfulness
The doctrine of eternal security
The doctrine of universal salvation
The doctrine of free will without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment and the enforcement of covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Solomon's actions against Adonijah and Abiathar demonstrate divine judgment against those who oppose God's anointed king and the enforcement of covenant faithfulness, fulfilling the LORD's word concerning the priesthood and kingship (1 Kings 2:24-27).

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 2:10-11 contribute to the biblical narrative arc concerning David's kingship?
options: It marks the end of an era and the transition to Solomon’s reign, fulfilling God's promises to David
It introduces the division of the kingdom into Israel and Judah
It records David’s conquest of Jerusalem
It highlights the building of the Temple
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the end of an era and the transition to Solomon’s reign, fulfilling God's promises to David
questions.explanation: These verses record David’s death and burial, summarizing his 40-year reign, thus closing a chapter in Israel’s history and paving the way for Solomon’s reign, which fulfills God’s covenant promises to David (1 Kings 2:10-11).

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Solomon’s confident assertion of his kingdom’s establishment in 1 Kings 2:24?
options: God’s faithfulness in establishing His promises
God’s wrath against sinners
God’s patience with disobedient kings
God’s mystery and unknowability
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness in establishing His promises
questions.explanation: Solomon declares that the LORD who established him and set him on David’s throne fulfilled His promise to build a lasting house, revealing God’s faithfulness and covenant steadfastness (1 Kings 2:24).

questions.question: Considering 1 Kings 2:5-6 and 2:32, what combined doctrine concerning justice and retribution is taught regarding Joab?
options: God administers justice by holding individuals accountable for shedding innocent blood
Revenge is justified as a human duty
Kings should ignore past sins for peace
Justice is only temporal and not eternal
questions.correctAnswer: God administers justice by holding individuals accountable for shedding innocent blood
questions.explanation: David reminds Solomon of Joab’s unjust killings (1 Kings 2:5-6), and Solomon declares that Joab’s blood will return upon his own head because he slew two righteous men, emphasizing God’s justice in holding wrongdoers accountable (1 Kings 2:32).

questions.question: What theological significance does Solomon’s treatment of Shimei in 1 Kings 2:36-46 reveal about divine sovereignty and human responsibility?
options: God sovereignly ordains consequences, but humans are responsible to obey His commands
God arbitrarily punishes without reason
Human actions are irrelevant under divine sovereignty
God’s sovereignty excuses all human disobedience
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly ordains consequences, but humans are responsible to obey His commands
questions.explanation: Solomon warns Shimei not to leave Jerusalem lest he die; Shimei disobeys and dies, demonstrating that while God ordains consequences, humans bear responsibility for obedience (1 Kings 2:36-46).

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 2:7 demonstrate the doctrine of grace and kindness even amid judgments?
options: David instructs Solomon to show kindness to the sons of Barzillai who supported him in exile
David commands total destruction of all his enemies
David orders Solomon to exile all loyalists
David ignores past kindnesses in favor of strict justice
questions.correctAnswer: David instructs Solomon to show kindness to the sons of Barzillai who supported him in exile
questions.explanation: Despite the harsh judgments commanded in the chapter, David tells Solomon to show kindness to Barzillai’s sons because they provided support during David’s flight, illustrating grace alongside justice (1 Kings 2:7).

questions.question: What does Solomon’s interaction with Bathsheba regarding Adonijah’s request (1 Kings 2:19-23) reveal about the nature of royal authority and wisdom?
options: Solomon exercises discerning royal authority by rejecting a request that threatens his reign
Solomon immediately grants every petition without question
Solomon defers all decisions to his mother
Solomon avoids conflict by ignoring requests
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon exercises discerning royal authority by rejecting a request that threatens his reign
questions.explanation: When asked to give Abishag to Adonijah, Solomon refuses and perceives it as a political threat, showing his wisdom and decisive authority to secure his throne (1 Kings 2:19-23).

questions.question: What does the instruction to bury Joab in his own house in the wilderness (1 Kings 2:34) signify about justice and honor in biblical context?
options: Even those executed for wrongdoing receive proper burial according to their status
Executions are followed by public humiliation
No burial is given to those who commit murder
Buries are only for the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: Even those executed for wrongdoing receive proper burial according to their status
questions.explanation: Joab was killed for his crimes but buried in his own house, indicating that biblical justice includes proper treatment in death even for wrongdoers, reflecting order and honor in judgment (1 Kings 2:34).

questions.question: How does David's charge to Solomon in 1 Kings 2:2-3 illustrate the biblical understanding of sanctification and maturity?
options: David exhorts Solomon to be strong and show himself a man by obeying God's law
David tells Solomon to rely solely on military strength
David encourages Solomon to seek personal wealth
David advises Solomon to disregard God's statutes
questions.correctAnswer: David exhorts Solomon to be strong and show himself a man by obeying God's law
questions.explanation: David charges Solomon to be strong and act like a man by faithfully keeping God's commandments, revealing sanctification as strength through obedience and maturity in faith (1 Kings 2:2-3).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God condones political murders in 1 Kings 2. What does 1 Kings 2:24-25 actually teach about God’s sovereignty and justice in the establishment of Solomon’s kingdom?
options: God sovereignly establishes His appointed king and enacts justice on those opposing His covenant
God randomly endorses violence without moral grounds
God ignores political events entirely
God permits all human actions without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly establishes His appointed king and enacts justice on those opposing His covenant
questions.explanation: These verses show Solomon executing judgment on Adonijah as part of God's sovereign plan to establish Solomon’s throne, indicating divine justice rather than arbitrary violence (1 Kings 2:24-25).

questions.question: What combined insight about covenant faithfulness and divine promise is drawn from 1 Kings 2:3 and 2:45?
options: Obedience to God's law leads to blessing and the establishment of David’s throne forever
God’s promises are unconditional regardless of obedience
The covenant is based on human effort alone
Blessings come only through military conquest
questions.correctAnswer: Obedience to God's law leads to blessing and the establishment of David’s throne forever
questions.explanation: David commands obedience to God's law for prosperity (2:3), and Solomon declares God's blessing and the throne's establishment forever (2:45), linking faithfulness with covenant fulfillment.

questions.question: How does the removal of Abiathar from the priesthood (1 Kings 2:26-27) reflect the doctrine of divine judgment and covenantal consequences?
options: It fulfills God's word against the house of Eli, showing judgment on unfaithful priesthood
It demonstrates human favoritism
It is an act of political convenience without spiritual significance
It shows that priests can act without consequences
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills God's word against the house of Eli, showing judgment on unfaithful priesthood
questions.explanation: Abiathar’s removal fulfills the LORD’s prophecy against Eli’s house, illustrating divine judgment and covenant consequences for unfaithfulness (1 Kings 2:26-27).

questions.question: What does Solomon’s elevation of Benaiah and Zadok in 1 Kings 2:35 teach about God’s providence in leadership transitions?
options: God providentially raises faithful servants to replace those removed
Leadership changes are purely political
New leaders are chosen randomly
Leaders gain position through force alone
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially raises faithful servants to replace those removed
questions.explanation: Solomon appoints Benaiah and Zadok, faithful servants, to key positions, showing God’s providential guidance in establishing righteous leadership (1 Kings 2:35).
